display.title: Episode 22: The Needles and Toothpicks, Chapter 1 (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: Counting the Omer toward Shavuos, Shema with the whole family, and a king's question about idol worship answered with a story of a son who keeps buying worthless bargains.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 11 Iyar 5742, the 26th day of the Omer. Uncle Yossi explains that the Jewish people counted the days from Egypt to Mount Sinai out of eagerness to receive the Torah, which is 'our Torah' because we said 'we will do and we will listen'. The remaining 23 days are for self-improvement: more respect for parents, elders and teachers, and real friendship, so we receive the Torah with joy and come to the greatest joy, the Geulah. A listener's letter about saying the Shema with her whole family leads to a lesson on sharing mitzvos, and a girl from a Boro Park Beis Yaakov leads the Shema. The story begins with the first two of the Ten Commandments: a friendly king asks a rabbi why Hashem warns only the Jews so strictly against idol worship. The rabbi answers with a story: a devoted father gives his son 2,000 gold coins to start a business, but the son buys a trainload of toothpicks with no points, and then, given a second chance, a trainload of needles with no eyes. A surprising, funny ending is promised for next week. The show ends with a mezuzah drawing, The Moshiach Times, and how to join Tzivos Hashem.
display.lesson: Use the days of Sefirah to improve yourself and prepare to receive the Torah with joy; share your mitzvos with others.

date.note: 'Today, which is the 11th day of the month Iyar, is also the 26th day of the Omer'; next week is Lag BaOmer.
